questions.question: A metropolitan city plans a high-speed elevated highway corridor. This project benefits private car owners by cutting commute times, but destroys the shops and livelihoods of roadside vendors and small shopkeepers. This scenario demonstrates:
options: Elevated expressways eliminate poverty for all citizens automatically
Roadside vendors should be barred from using judicial courts
Urban planning is legally exempted from constitutional review
Developmental goals can be mutually conflicting; what represents development for one section can cause economic displacement for another
questions.explanation: People have conflicting developmental goals. An urban commuter benefits from elevated flyovers, but small roadside vendors lose their shops and livelihoods when land is acquired, creating conflict between different social groups.

questions.question: A young engineer is offered two jobs: Job A offers very high pay but no job security and long erratic hours leaving no time for family; Job B offers slightly lower pay but regular hours, permanent job security, and health insurance for family. If she chooses Job B, it proves that:
options: High salaries are legally prohibited in private software corporations
People look at a mix of goals including job security, working environment, and work-life balance, not just monetary salary alone
Engineers are irrational economic decision makers
Job security is irrelevant to modern professionals
questions.explanation: If women or men are engaged in paid work, their dignity increases. But people look at a mix of goals: working environment, opportunity to learn, sense of security, and freedom are as critical as monetary salary.

questions.subtopic: Country Comparison: Equal vs Unequal Incomes
questions.question: Consider two countries X and Y with 5 citizens each, both having an average income of ₹10,000. In Country X, individual incomes are ₹9,500, ₹10,500, ₹9,800, ₹10,000, and ₹10,200. In Country Y, incomes are ₹500, ₹500, ₹500, ₹500, and ₹48,000. Which country would an equitable citizen prefer to live in?
options: Country X, because income is equitably distributed with neither extreme riches nor abject poverty
Country Y, because it has one ultra-wealthy billionaire who can buy luxury yachts
Country Y, because 80% of citizens are guaranteed to remain poor
Both countries are identical in every social and human dimension
questions.explanation: Even though both countries have the same average income (₹10,000), Country X is preferred because income is equitably distributed. In Country Y, four citizens are destitute while one person monopolizes nearly all wealth.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Economics, Chapter 1, Section 1.3, Table 1.2

questions.question: Why does the World Bank and UNDP calculate per capita income in 'Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) Dollars' rather than nominal exchange rates?
options: Because nominal dollars are legally invalid in developing Asian countries
Because the United Nations only accepts gold coins for calculations
Because one dollar must be able to purchase the same quantity of goods and services in any country, eliminating currency price distortions
Because PPP dollars automatically double the national income of rich nations
questions.explanation: Per capita income is calculated in international dollars (PPP) so that one dollar buys the same basket of goods and services in any country, providing a fair standard of comparison.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Economics, Chapter 1, Section 1.4 (Footnote on PPP)

questions.question: According to official data in NCERT Table 1.4, nearly half of children aged 14–15 in Bihar are not attending school beyond Class 8. What does this imply for Bihar's human development?
options: Bihar has achieved universal literacy in technical university degrees
A significant demographic proportion is deprived of secondary education, severely limiting future skilled employment opportunities and state development
Children in Bihar are legally barred from entering secondary schools
Bihar requires all teenagers to serve in the state police brigade
questions.explanation: In Bihar, around half of the children aged 14-15 are not attending school beyond Class 8. This means that if you went to school in Bihar, nearly half of your elementary cohort would be missing, indicating serious underdevelopment of human capital.

questions.question: In states like Tamil Nadu and Kerala, where the Public Distribution System (PDS) functions efficiently, surveys show that:
options: The health and nutritional status of the rural poor is significantly better than in states with dysfunctional PDS
Food grains in fair price shops remain unsold and rot in warehouses
Agricultural farmers refuse to cultivate paddy crops
The poverty rate rises by 50% every year
questions.explanation: In some states, the PDS functions well. In these states, the health and nutritional status of people is certainly likely to be better because cheap, subsidized food grains are regularly available to low-income families.

questions.question: A 25-year-old adult weighs 50 kg and is 1.60 meters tall. What is the individual's BMI, and what does it indicate about their nutritional status? (1.60² = 2.56)
options: BMI ≈ 15.20 kg/m²; the individual is severely undernourished
BMI ≈ 31.25 kg/m²; the individual is clinically obese
BMI ≈ 10.50 kg/m²; the individual requires immediate medical hospitalization
BMI ≈ 19.53 kg/m²; the individual falls in the normal, healthy nutritional range
questions.explanation: BMI = Weight / (Height)² = 50 / (1.60 × 1.60) = 50 / 2.56 ≈ 19.53. Since 19.53 is between 18.5 and 25, the person is within the normal and healthy nutritional range.

questions.question: According to World Energy Review data cited in NCERT, global crude oil reserves are estimated to last roughly 50 years at current extraction rates. What serious developmental implication arises?
options: Crude oil prices will drop to zero permanently
Internal combustion engines will run on sea water automatically
Countries like India, which import over 80% of their crude oil, face severe economic vulnerability unless renewable energy alternatives are rapidly developed
Automobile transportation will be permanently banned globally by 2030
questions.explanation: India depends on importing oil from abroad because it does not have enough stocks of its own. If oil prices increase this becomes a burden for everyone. Moreover, non-renewable energy exhaustion threatens long-term sustainable development.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Economics, Chapter 1, Section 1.5, Table 1.7

questions.question: Why is collective provision of public services (e.g., municipal security, government schools) economically more sensible than individual private provision?
options: Private individuals are legally forbidden from purchasing private solar panels
Collective provision guarantees that no public funds will ever be spent
It is vastly cheaper and more effective to provide community services collectively than for every individual house to hire private guards or set up private generators
Private companies refuse to sell security alarms to homeowners
questions.explanation: Actually for many of the important things in life the best way, also the cheapest way, is to provide these goods and services collectively. Just think — will it be cheaper to have collective security for the whole locality or for each house to have its own security man?

questions.question: Surveys in rural India often reveal that women and young girls have significantly higher rates of low BMI (< 18.5) than men. What underlying socio-economic factor causes this?
options: Genetic inability of rural women to digest food grains
Government laws mandating that women fast five days a week
Higher physical metabolism of women compared to male field labourers
Intra-household nutritional discrimination where women eat last and least after serving other family members
questions.explanation: Sociological and economic surveys indicate that gender bias in intra-household food distribution, where women eat after male members and receive smaller shares of nutritious food, leads to higher female undernourishment.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Economics, Chapter 1, Section 1.4 (Activity 3 Analysis)

questions.subtopic: Middle East Oil Wealth vs Human Development
questions.question: Why are several oil-rich Middle Eastern nations excluded from the category of 'developed countries' despite having extremely high per capita incomes?
options: Because they refuse to use US dollars in petroleum trade
Because high income is derived almost entirely from oil rents rather than diversified human capabilities, and educational/gender development lags behind
Because their total geographical land area is less than 500 square kilometers
Because the United Nations disallows monarchies from receiving developed status
questions.explanation: Countries with per capita income above the rich country threshold, excluding countries of Middle East and certain other small countries, are generally called developed countries because high development requires equitable social, educational, and political freedoms alongside wealth.

questions.question: 'Consequences of environmental degradation do not respect national or state boundaries.' Which real-world example best validates this principle?
options: Air pollution from stubble burning or greenhouse gas emissions warming global oceans affects neighbouring states and entire continents regardless of borders
Municipal water taxes collected in Delhi are transferred to Sri Lanka
Earthquake shocks only travel through countries that have signed the Paris Climate Accord
Acid rain only falls on privately owned industrial factories
questions.explanation: Our future is linked together. Sustainability of development is a new area of knowledge in which scientists, economists, philosophers and other social scientists are working together because environmental crises (climate change, air pollution, ozone depletion) transcend political boundaries.

questions.subtopic: Girl Child Education in Rural India
questions.question: In many rural districts of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, girls drop out after Class 5 because:
options: Government has not provided adequate secondary schools or safe transport nearby, and society does not yet value female schooling equally
Girls are legally disqualified from learning arithmetic and science
Secondary school teachers refuse to teach female students
School textbooks are written exclusively in foreign languages
questions.explanation: Many girls are not able to achieve secondary level schooling because government/society has not provided adequate facilities. Where local schools and public transport are established, female enrolment rises dramatically.

questions.subtopic: Comparing Haryana and Kerala Health Metrics
questions.question: Haryana had a per capita income of ₹1,80,174 compared to Kerala's ₹1,63,476 (2016-17 data), but Kerala's IMR was only 10 per 1,000 live births compared to Haryana's 30. What does this contrast teach us?
options: Haryana residents prefer not to take sick infants to hospitals
Higher personal income does not guarantee superior public health or child survival unless the state invests systematically in primary healthcare infrastructure
Per capita income in Kerala is completely inaccurate and fabricated
Infant mortality has no relationship to medical infrastructure or nursing care
questions.explanation: Even though Haryana is wealthier in terms of average per capita income, an infant born in Haryana is three times more likely to die before age one than in Kerala, proving that public health infrastructure and social development are independent of mere income.
questions.citation: NCERT Class 10 Economics, Chapter 1, Section 1.4, Tables 1.3 & 1.4

questions.question: 'National Development' encompasses which of the following comprehensive objectives?
options: Constructing the largest presidential palace in the world
Doubling the national debt by purchasing foreign luxury automobiles
Improving the living standards of citizens, providing food security, healthcare, education, and reducing social and economic inequalities
Banning all foreign books and newspapers from public libraries
questions.explanation: National development means thinking about fair and just paths for all, whether there is a better way of doing things, and ensuring that development benefits the largest number of people equitably.

questions.question: Which three dimensions are aggregated to calculate the Human Development Index (HDI)?
options: Military size, national gold reserves, and total highway kilometres
Annual steel production, number of airports, and coal consumption
Population density, agricultural land acreage, and foreign exchange reserves
Decent standard of living (GNI per capita), knowledge (mean and expected years of schooling), and long and healthy life (life expectancy)
questions.explanation: HDI is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic dimensions of human development: a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living.

questions.question: Which regions in India are experiencing the most critical depletion of underground water tables?
options: Agriculturally prosperous regions of Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh, and hard-rock plateau areas of central and southern India
The Thar desert sand dunes of Western Rajasthan
The glaciated mountain peaks of Ladakh
The mangrove swamps of the Sundarbans in West Bengal
questions.explanation: Groundwater overuse is particularly found in the agriculturally prosperous regions of Punjab and Western U.P., hard rock plateau areas of central and south India, some coastal areas and rapidly growing urban settlements.

questions.question: Why is the exploitation of non-renewable fossil fuels inherently incompatible with indefinite economic growth?
options: Because petroleum turns into gold after fifty years of underground storage
Because foreign governments can confiscate underground oil reserves remotely
Because fossil fuel reserves are finite and their combustion generates severe carbon emissions driving climate change and ecological collapse
Because fossil fuels cannot be transported through steel pipelines
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are finite; once consumed, they cannot be regenerated on a human timescale, and their excessive usage causes atmospheric pollution and global warming, undermining sustainable development.

questions.question: When assessing whether an individual is living below the poverty line, economists consider not just monetary income but also:
options: Whether the individual owns a four-bedroom luxury penthouse
Daily minimum nutritional caloric intake (2,400 calories in rural and 2,100 calories in urban areas) and access to essential clothing, shelter, and healthcare
How many international vacation flights the person takes each year
The number of designer wristwatches in the household
questions.explanation: Poverty measurement in India combines minimum income levels with basic nutritional calorie benchmarks (2,400 cal rural, 2,100 cal urban) and essential physical provisions necessary for survival.

questions.question: Nobel laureate Amartya Sen's approach to development, reflected in NCERT Economics, defines development fundamentally as:
options: The accumulation of high monetary foreign exchange balances in central banks
Maximizing industrial smokestacks and factory output at any environmental cost
Eliminating all political debate in favor of technocratic decrees
The expansion of human freedoms and capabilities to lead lives people have reason to value
questions.explanation: Development is fundamentally about expanding human capabilities — literacy, good health, freedom from avoidable disease, and social empowerment — enabling people to lead dignified, fulfilling lives.
